3. Scope of Service 
 
3.1. WIC Services: 
 
The WIC Program Contractor shall perform all the work required to administer and provide WIC services to 
eligible participants according to the Arizona WIC Program Policies and Procedures Manual (WIC PPM). These 
include, but are not limited to, the following activities: 
 
3.1.1. Perform WIC certification procedures such as categorical and income screening and health and 
nutrition assessments, 
 
3.1.2. Provide participant centered nutrition and breastfeeding support services to WIC participants, 
 
3.1.3. Provide the mandatory and appropriate additional referrals reflecting the needs of the individual WIC 
participants, 
 
3.1.4. Issue WIC food benefits tailored to meet the needs of the participants, 
 
3.1.5. Ensure the collection and recording of accurate information, 
 
3.1.6. Provide p rofessional training, mentoring and monitoring of WIC staff competencies necessary for 
delivery of required services, 
 
3.1.7. Provide administrative functions for operation of the WIC Program, and 
 
3.1.8. Prepare and submit all required plans/reports in accordance with this contract and the WIC PPM. 
 
3.2. BFPC Services: 
 
3.2.1. WIC BFPC Contractors shall perform all the work required to administer and provide additional 
breastfeeding support services to WIC mothers following the USDA WIC Breastfeeding Curriculum 
guidelines for peer counseling services and according to the Contractor’s proposal in order to increase 
the breastfeeding rate and duration of breastfeeding, and 
 
3.2.2. Provide supervision, mentoring, monitoring, and evaluation of peer counselors, when appropriate. 
 
4. Tasks 
 
The Contractor shall: 
 
4.1. WIC Services Outreach, Retention, and Referrals: 
 
4.1.1. Conduct outreach activities targeting underserved populations by developing written and verbal 
presentations, or utilizing available materials, and/or promoting WIC on social media platforms to 
inform potentially WIC eligible individuals of the availability of the WIC Program and to explain the 
benefits of participation in accordance with the WIC PPM and this Contract, 
 
4.1.2. Conduct retention activities to maintain and increase the participation of current WIC enrollees, 
 
4.1.3. Establish community partnerships with, at a minimum, the mandatory referral agencies, local hospitals, 
OB/GYN and pediatricians offices, and provide regular contacts in accordance with the WIC PPM and 
this Contract,

4.1.5. Establish a referral system with breastfeeding/lactation specialists, including , but not limited to, 
International Board-Certified Lactation Consultants (IBCLC), Certified Lactation Counselors (CLC), 
Certified Breastfeeding Counselors (CBC), and Certified Lactation Educators (CLE) in accordance

4.3.6. Ensure paper files containing confidential participant information are stored in a secure location in 
the clinic, archived when appropriate, and destroyed according to the retention schedule.  All files 
should be destroyed in an appropriate manner, 
 
4.3.7. The Local Agency shall notify the State Agency immediately by telephone call and email upon the 
discovery of a breach of a participant’s confidentiality, 
 
4.3.8. Local Agency shall immediately investigate such security incident, breach, or unauthorized use or 
disclosure of participant information. These investigations shall include: 
 
4.3.8.1. What data elements were involved and the extent of the data involved in the breach; 
 
4.3.8.2. A description of the unauthorized person(s) known or reasonably believed to have 
improperly used or disclosed the protected information; 
 
4.3.8.3. A description of where the protected information is believed to have been improperly 
transmitted, sent, or utilized; 
 
4.3.8.4. A description of the probable causes of the improper use or disclosure; and 
 
4.3.8.5. Whether Arizona Revised Statutes (A.R.S) § 18-545 or any other federal or state laws 
requiring individual notifications of breaches are triggered. 
 
4.3.9. The Local Agency shall provide a written report of the investigation to the Chief of the BNPA/WIC 
Director and Program Integrity Manager within ten (10) working days of the discovery of the breach 
or unauthorized use or disclosure.  The report sha ll include the information specified above, as 
well as a full, detailed corrective action plan, including information on measures that were taken 
to halt and/or contain the improper use or disclosure, and 
 
4.3.10. The Local Agency shall notify individuals of the b reach or unauthorized use or disclosure when 
notification is required under state or federal law and shall pay any costs of such notifications, as 
well as any costs associated with the breach using non -WIC funds. The Chief of the BNPA/WIC 
Director, Program  Integrity Manager, and Assistant Attorney General shall approve the time, 
manner and content of any such notifications. The Local Agency shall arrange and pay for any 
mitigation (e.g. LifeLock) for participants at risk for identity theft because of breach  of security of 
information. 
 
4.4. Service Delivery and Program Rules: 
 
4.4.1. Determine eligibility of persons requesting WIC services by screening individuals in accordance with 
procedures set forth in the WIC PPM. 
 
4.4.2. Eligible program participants shall include the following categories whose household income does not 
exceed 185% of the current designated federal poverty guidelines, who have a nutritional risk as 
defined in the WIC PPM, and reside in Arizona as defined by the WIC PPM: 
  
4.4.2.1. Pregnant women, breastfeeding women up to twelve (12) months post-partum, and 
non-breastfeeding women up to six (6) months following the end of a pregnancy; 
 
4.4.2.2. Infants from birth to age one (1); and 
 
4.4.2.3. Children from age one (1) year up to five (5) years. 
 
4.4.3. Provide complete nutrition assessment and document results and follow-up as outlined in chapter 
two (2) and seven (7) of the Arizona WIC Policy and Procedure Manual,

refer to and promote the Breastfeeding Peer Counseling Program, when appropriate, 
 
4.4.7. Prescribe and tailor a food package appropriate to the participant's nutritional risk(s), the amount 
of formula consumed, and cultural preferences and issue food benefits as set forth in the WIC 
PPM, 
 
4.4.8. Provide program participants with information about available health and social services to which 
the participant could be referred. The participant shall be provided with written information

referral procedures, 
 
4.4.9. Coordinate WIC Services with other health and social services available within the service area,

4.4.10. Provide information, check for understanding, and document instruction to participants on program 
rules, regulations, WIC approved foods, use of eWIC cards, and food benefit use and redemption. 
The program instruction shall be documented in the participant's record as set forth in the WIC 
PPM, and

and WIC applicants’ access to services.

Authorized Representatives of infant and child participants certified. Nutrition education contacts shall 
be scheduled on a periodic basis by the local agency, but such contacts do not necessarily need to 
take place in each quarter of the certification period,

WIC PPM Local Agencies may designate a Bachelor's degree nutritionist or Nutrition and Dietetic

administration.  With prior approval from ADHS, number of years working in a WIC p rogram may

coordination of nutrition services within the Local Agency to be approved by ADHS,

9. Performance Standards and Award Program 
 
9.1. Upon Contract finalization, ADHS shall notify the Contractor by email of the assigned caseload and, throughout 
the term of the Contract, any changes to the assigned caseload. The Contractor shall maintain an average 
monthly participation level in accordance with the following table: 
 
Caseload Assignment    % Maintained 
<10,000 participants/month    97% 
10,000 to <49,999 participants/month   98% 
>50,000 participants/month    99% 
 
9.2. If, after each quarter of the Federal Fiscal Year (October through September), the Contractor has not attained 
the required participation level, ADHS will have the option of reducing the assigned caseload and resources to 
the Contractor's current service level. ADHS may then move the unused caseload and corresponding resources 
to other WIC Local Agencies in order to fully utilize the resources; 
 
9.3. Local Agencies shall be eligible for one (1) or more of the following awards: 
 
9.3.1. Any local agency which meets 100% or more of its caseload assignment for three (3) consecutive 
months during the previous FFY may receive an award of $10,000 added to that agency's following 
fiscal year WIC funding formula award if the Contract is extended and additional expenditures can be 
identified, 
 
9.3.2. Utilizing the “Nutrition Discussion Contact” report ran in the first quarter of the FFY preceding time of 
application (October through December), any Local Agency meeting ninety-five percent (95%) of its 
nutrition education documentation requirement for each participation time period may receive an 
award of $10,000 added to that agency's following fiscal year WIC funding formula award if the 
Contract is extended and additional expenditures can be identified,

Proposal for Technical Adjustment to Justice of the Precinct Boundaries 
 
Issue and Background:    During the process of drawing election precincts staff noticed 
a slight misalignment of the justice of the peace precincts.  The impacted area is very 
small and is northeast of Winslow Arizona but south of the Navajo Nation Boundary.   
Staff recommends fixing the misalignment. 
 
Impact on Public Safety:    No impacts to public safety are anticipated. 
 
Impact on Residents:   There are no residents that reside in the area impacted by the 
boundary change.  As no residents live in the impacted census blocks, there are no 
changes to the percentage of minority populations in the impacted justice of the peace 
precincts. 
 
Impact on the Justice Courts:   The change will have no impact on caseloads or judicial 
productivity credits

RESOLUTION NO. __________ 
 
A RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF NAVAJO 
COUNTY, ARIZONA, ADOPTING A NEW VOTING PRECINCT MAP 
AND POLLING PLACES PURSUANT TO A.R.S. § 16-411 
 
WHEREAS, A.R.S. § 16-411 requires the Board of Supervisors to meet on or before 
October 1 of each year preceding the year of a general election for the purpose of establishing a 
convenient number of election precincts in the county and defining the boundaries of those 
precincts; and 
 
WHEREAS,  pursuant to A.R.S. 11-212 and A.R.S. 15-1441 (A), the Board on March 
22, 2022 adopted new Supervisorial District boundaries and Northland Pioneer Community 
Collage Precincts; and  
 
WHEREAS, the Board of Supervisors adopted interim election precincts on  or about 
September 26, 2023; and 
 
WHEREAS, the County has modified its justice of the peace precincts and needs and 
finalize its election precincts in conformity therewith; and 
 
WHEREAS, County staff have made recommendations to the Board regarding new 
precinct lines that would (1) be consistent with the new redistricting plans adopted by the 
County, (2) eliminate voter confusion, (3) enhance the efficient use of County election resources, 
(4) accomplish all of the foregoing without any significant inconvenient to any group of voters in 
the County. 
 
 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board as follows: 
 
1.)  That a new precinct map and updated boundaries attached hereto and incorporated 
herein as “Exhibit A.”  are hereby approved by the Navajo County Board of 
Supervisors. 
 
2.)  The polling places and/or voting centers to be utilized for each of these precincts will 
be established pursuant to procedures set forth A.R.S. §16-411(B), herein as “Exhibit 
B”

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. a. 1. a.        
Meeting Date: 10/24/2023  
Title: IGA between NCFCD and the City of Show Low for City Park Drainage
Improvement Project
Submitted For: Madhav Mundle, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Donald Perkins, Flood Control Manager
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Donald Perkins
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of Intergovernmental Agreement between Navajo County Flood Control District
and the City of Show Low for financial assistance for the City Park Drainage Improvement
Project in the amount of $140,000. 
Background:
The City of Show Low is requesting financial assistance with their City Park Drainage
Improvement Project.  The purpose of this IGA is to authorize the County to partner financially,
as the County and the City share a common interest to improve residential drainage areas
downstream of Show Low City Park to help reduce the chance of future flooding. The City is
requesting financial assistance from the Navajo County Flood Control District to reimburse the
City based on paid invoices to the contractor. Payment to the City will be consistent with
progress payments made to the contractor.  The City shall be solely responsible for the design,
procurement, permitting, and construction of the Project. The City understands and agrees that
the County’s sole participation and obligation with respect to the Project shall be to provide
finance assistance in the amount not to exceed $140,000.  Public Works has reviewed the
request and finds it consistent with the purpose of the Flood Control District and supports the
Project.  
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends the execution of this IGA
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: 24
Budgeted Y/N: Y

Intergovernmental Agreement for 
Flood Control Project Funding 
 
THIS INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGREEMENT is entered into as of October 24, 2023 (“Effective 
Date”) by and between the Navajo County Flood Control District, a special taxing district organized 
pursuant to Title 48, Chapter 21 of the Arizona Revised Statutes (“the District”), and the City of 
Show Low, an Arizona municipal corporation (“the City”). 
1. Premises. 
1.1        The parties are authorized to enter into intergovernmental agreements for joint or 
cooperative action pursuant to A.R.S § 11-952. 
1.2      The City has identified an area within its boundaries where its stormwater system is 
not functioning properly. 
1.3      The City has engaged the services of Ironside Engineering & Development (IE&D) for 
two items: 
1. Determine the cause(s) of flooding due to the inadequate stormwater system 
2. Design a  detention basin to help reduce flooding in the  residential area s                           
downstream from Show Low City Park in Navajo County. 
      1.4      The City is ready to proceed with construction on the City Park Drainage Improvement 
Project to correct the stormwater drainage deficiencies and the City is requesting 
$140,000 financial assistance from the Navajo County Flood Control District.  
      1.5      The City of Show Low shall bid this project, based on a preliminary cost estimate and 
provide Navajo County Flood Control District with a copy of the executed contract with 
the contractor. The District will reimburse the City based on paid invoices to the 
Contractor not to exceed $140,000. Payments to the City will be consistent with 
progress payments made to the Contractor and within 30 days. 
     1.6        The District is authorized by A.R.S § 48-3603(C)(3) to contract and join with a 
municipality such as the City “in acquiring constructing, maintaining and 
operating flood control works, and regulating floodplains.” 
     1.7      The Board of Directors of the District has determined that it is an appropriate use of 
District funds to financially assist the City with this Project and has budgeted an amount 
not to exceed $140,000 for this purp ose, subject to the terms and conditions of this 
agreement.

<!-- page 635 -->
2 
 
2.    The District’s Obligations. 
       2.1     The District shall reimburse the City for eligible costs of this Project, up to a maximum 
reimbursement of $140,000.  Eligible costs are the actual expenses of construction 
materials and supplies and other contractual services directly associated with this 
Project, property acquisition directly associated with the Project, and construction and 
program management. The City’s administrative and other internal expenses are not 
eligible costs, no r are the expenses of improvements not directly related to flood 
control such as landscaping. 
 
3.     Indemnification. 
        3.1     To the fullest extent permissible by law, the City shall indemnify, defend and hold 
harmless the District and its officers, employees and agents from and against any and 
all claims, actions, suits, liabilities, damages, losses and expenses arising out  of the 
design, procurement, permitting and construction of the Project or the subsequent 
maintenance, repair or operation of Project facilities. 
 
4.     General. 
        4.1.1   This Agreement shall be effective as of the Effective Date and shall remain i n effect 
until this Project has been substantially completed. 
        4.1.2   Requests for reimbursement, payment and other communications relating to this 
Agreement shall be sent to the intended recipient at the following address. Either 
party may specify a different address by written notice to the other party: 
If to the District:                                                                         If to the City:

        4.1.3    In the event of any dispute arising out of this Agreement, the parties agree to make a 
good faith attempt to informally resolve or mediate the dispute before submitting the 
matter to arbitration pursuant to the provisions of A.R.S § 12-1518. 
 
        4.1.4    Each party warrants that this Agreement has been duly au thorized by its governing 
body, that the officials executing this Agreement on its behalf have been duly

       4.1.5     The provisions of A.R.S § 38-511 are incorporated herein by this reference. 
 
       4.1.6     This Agreement constitutes the entire understanding between the parties with respect 
to its subject matter, superseding any prior or contemporaneous agreements, 
whether oral or written, concerning the same subject matter. This Agreement may be

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. b. 1.        
Meeting Date: 10/24/2023  
Title: SUP 23-011 US-AZ-5117 Silver Creek Wireless Communication Facility - District
III
Submitted By: Cody Cooper, Planning Manager
Department: Public Works Division: Planning & Development
Presented By: Cody Cooper
Motion before the Board:
PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration of adoption of Resolution Number
41-2023, approving/denying a Special Use Permit to allow for the construction of a 80’
rusticated monopole wireless communication tower and associated facilities on a vacant,
2.50-acre parcel, in the White Mountain Lakes area.
Background:
The subject parcel is lot 328 of the White Mountain Lakes Unit 11 Subdivision, originally
designated as a community area.
This property currently has a building which is utilized as a community center, library, and U.S.
Post Office.
At the Thursday, September 21st, 2023 Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission
Hearing, the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously recommended
denial of this project.
 
Recommendation: 
The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously recommended denial of
this Special Use Permit
Based upon the fact that this proposal does not meet all relevant goals of the Navajo County
Comprehensive Plan and requires a waiver to setback standards which can only be granted by
the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, Planning and Development Services Staff
recommends denial of this Special Use Permit.
If the Navajo County Board of Supervisors approves this Special Use Permit, Navajo County
Planning and Development Services Staff would recommend the conditions that are outlined in
the Staff Report.

PROJECT NARRATIVE 
 
FOR 
 
Vertical Bridge US-AZ-5117 Silver Creek  
80’ Multi-Carrier Communications Pole 
 
1785 Edmonds Circle 
Show Low, AZ 85901 
APN: 304-34-328 
Jurisdiction:  Navajo County

Yellow Pins denote existing Verizon sites.  Proposed Vertical Bridge site is Green Pin 
 
Submitted by:

22831 N. 21st St

<!-- page 650 -->
Purpose of Application 
 
As part of its ongoing effort to maintain the pre-eminent wireless network in Navajo County, 
Verizon Wireless has engaged Vertical Bridge to develop several sites within the County to improve 
coverage and capacity for Verizon’s network.  This approach is being used to allow for the County to be 
built out faster than if Verizon was developing the sites directly.  Vertical Bridge is one of a few companies 
who have been engaged for different locations throughout the County as part of an overall development 
plan meant to improve rural broadband and overall connectivity.  Vertical Bridge is a large tower 
development and management firm with sites throughout the Country and many within Arizona.   
 
This proposal is for a new site in the White Mountain Lake Estates neighborhood.  This site is 
meant to work in conjunction with the existing site to the west at Juniper Ridge.  As I stated at the time 
when we went through the Special Use Permit process for the pole at Juniper Ridge, there would likely 
need to be a new site a few miles east to provide in-building coverage to folks in the eastern part of this 
development.  That is what we are now proposing.   
 
This site is meant to ensure good in-building coverage in this area as well as offer some 
improvement heading north and south along Bourdon Ranch Road.  White Mountain Lakes Estates has 
coverage which drops off quickly on its eastern side as it is currently served by the site at Juniper Ridge.  
Verizon has requested this site to become the primary serving site for the area.  This site will have a 
secondary benefit of offloading capacity at Juniper Ridge which should improve the performance of that 
site for the folks near Juniper Ridge.  It also will integrate with a future site which will be along Bourdon 
Ranch north of the Airport and another site several miles southeast along Bourdon Ranch Road.   
 
While the anchor tenant will be Verizon Wireless, the structure is being developed to handle 
additional carriers if they choose to use it in the future.  CellOne does have a tower a bit over a mile west 
of this location so they would not likely need to collocate but there are two other carriers operating in this 
market. 
 
The primary focus for coverage and capacity was in more densely populated areas and along 
major thoroughfares within the last 5-10 years.  As areas such as this have become more populated and 
technologies have advanced, it is becoming necessary to build additional structures to accommodate 
coverage for residents, visitors and travelers in these areas.  This is a pretty dense area with homes on 
small lots.  Capacity is an issue on the west side of White Mountain Lakes Estates and coverage is an 
issue in the homes on the east side.  This site will help with both of those problems. 
 
 Due to the size and location of the pole at Juniper Ridge it can’t effectively service this area.  The 
existing tower owned by CellOne at the Fire Station is in a spot which makes it a poor option for 
collocation.  It is too close to Juniper Ridge and would overpower that site and is too far from the east side 
of White Mountain Estates to provide the in-building coverage the carrier needs from this site.  As noted 
above, this was discussed when Juniper Ridge went through the zoning process.  The plan has always 
been to place multiple sites in this area.    
 
A before and after coverage map has been included with this submittal to demonstrate the 
anticipated coverage improvements for Verizon Wireless.  Verizon’s plan consists of the site at Juniper 
Ridge, a site currently in development along Bourdon Ranch Road a few miles southeast of the community 
as well as another site along Bourdon Ranch Road on the north end of the community.  Two of these 
planned sites are being developed by Vertical Bridge at Verizon’s request.  The third site is being 
developed on the north side of the community by another tower vendor at Verizon’s request. 
 
 Vertical Bridge is requesting a Special Use Permit for a 80’ tall multi-carrier wireless monopole 
within a 50’ x 50’ compound.  There will be ground equipment within the compound.  The height has been 
reduced from the previously proposed 99’ to adhere to the new Wireless Ordinance.

<!-- page 651 -->
Site Description 
 
The subject parcel is just over 2.5 acres and is surrounded entirely by Edmonds Circle with homes 
on the parcels on the outside of the circle.  This parcel is owned by the Association and used for the 
Community Center/Library as well as the US Post Office.  The Parcel is zoned R1-10 but is one of the few 
non-residential uses in the development.  It is also one of the largest parcels in the development.     
 
The compound will be just east and southeast of the existing building with the community Center 
and the Post office.  This was done to cluster it with the existing buildings yet put it a reasonable distance 
from the surrounding road and homes beyond.  The location allows the pole to be about as far from 
neighboring homes as possible and it is close to the center of the parcel.    
 
Site History 
 
Verizon Wireless has been working on providing coverage in Navajo County for many years.  That 
often involves a few sites every year.  Now that 5G is being deployed to provide rural broadband coverage 
throughout much of Navajo County, Verizon has a need for several sit es within the next year or two.  
Verizon approached several tower developers about different sites throughout the County.  Vertical Bridge 
is one of the two main tower developers and current ly i s looking at this site.   Th e east side of this 
community is a targeted location requested by Verizon.   
 
As noted above, Verizon previously developed a site at Juniper Ridge two miles to the west.  It was 
always expected a future site would be needed, especially as technology advanced.  The original proposed 
location by the carrier was actu ally further east near  Bourdon Ranch Road.   Unfortunately, there is v ery 
little private land in that area, the parcels are very small and there would likely be issues  with the airstrip.    
When I spoke with the engineer to determine the desired coverage it became clear that this location would 
work to achieve the objectives, but we couldn’t really move any further west as it would begin encroaching 
on and overlapping the site at Juniper Ridge.  Moving north would overlap the site being developed on the 
north end of the community and moving south would land on undeveloped Sta te Land and quickly be 
overpowered by the site going to the southeast, as well as being much less effective within the community.   
 
I began looking at property records and noticed this parcel owned by t he Association.  It was a 
logical choice as a non-residential use and it also gave  the neighbors an additional opportunity to provide 
feedback on the design.  I devel oped a proposal for the location to keep the pole as far from the homes  
across the circle as reasonably possibl e.  The site was approved, Vertical Bridge entered into a Lease 
agreement with the Association and we are now moving forward with the entitlement process. 
 
Description of Proposal 
 
The proposed site development includes placement of panel antennas on a new 80’ monopole.  
The panel antennas are used for coverage to communicate with phones and other devices.  The 80’ is 
meant to provide a site which meets the needs of Verizon but does leave additional space for one to two 
carriers to collocate in the future.  Verizon’s antennas will be at 76’ on the pole to maximize integration with 
the site at Juniper Ridge, and the future sites to the southeast and north of the Airport.  The pole will be 
structurally capable of handling additional carriers and have usable space available within the compound.   
 
The proposed location is about as close as we could get to the center of the Association’s 2.5 acre 
parcel.  It is more than 1:1 from all property lines and the parcel is surrounded entirely by Edmonds Circle.  
An Engineer’s Letter has been received and provided with the application.  The site does not meet a 2:1 
setback and we are requesting relief based on the new Ordinance standards.  There is currently one home 
within 200’ of the pole location to the south and a total of 10 homes within 400’ of the proposed site.  There 
aren’t other locations within this development which would be able to keep the site further from homes.

<!-- page 652 -->
The location also is close to commercial power and appears to have fiber service available.  Access will 
come from Edmonds Circle through the existing parking lot.   
 
The 50’ x 50’ compound is located just ESE of the existing building.  The pole is in the center of the 
compound.  The pole exceeds a 1:1 setback from all property lines. 
   
The Verizon radio equipment will be on a small outdoor platform.  The site will have an emergency 
back-up generator.  The site has commercial power which will come from the existing power pole just SW 
of the main building on the property.  It appears that fiber backhaul is available as well.   
 
The site will take about 60-90 days to construct, and once complete, will be visited approximately 
once per month for maintenance.  This development is unoccupied and does not involve water or sewer.  
There will not be any changes to existing watercourses or an impact on off-site discharge of rainwater.     
   
 
 
 
Citizen Participation Plan 
 
As previously noted, this site has already been considered and approved by the White Mountain 
Lakes Estates Association.  Information about the site was distributed to the community and, very early in 
this process, I attended one of their meetings to answer questions regarding this proposal.  Those in 
attendance seemed in support of the idea.   
 
I have joined several of their meetings over the last few months and there are a few neighbors not 
in support of this proposal as well.  I have worked to provide information to the Association to forward to 
those opposed and indicated that a neighborhood meeting would likely be held to directly address any 
further questions they might have. 
 
I hosted a neighborhood meeting on July 27th and received feedback from residents.  This was 
noticed to residents within 300’ and the Association also distributed the notice on their Facebook page.  
The meeting was well attended and there were others watching and participating on a livestream of the 
event.  The majority of the attendees were opposed to the site based on health concerns.  Several of the 
attendees were in support of the site due to the need for improved coverage in the area.  I have included a 
detailed report and sign-in sheets with feedback from the meeting in the application submittal package.

<!-- page 653 -->
I also let the attendees know that the neighborhood meeting was really the first step in a process 
and they will have several more hearings at which they can be heard.  Notices for future meetings will be 
made as required by the Ordinance and will be given to the Association to distribute.  It seems the informal 
distribution by the Association is very good at getting the word out well beyond the standard notice area for 
a Use Permit. 
 
Conclusion 
 
This type of facility requires a Special Use Permit in Navajo County.  This proposal meets the letter 
and intent of the Ordinance, including the recently adopted language.  Vertical Bridge is requesting a 
Special Use Permit with a reduced setback requirement of 1:1 for this proposed site for the maximum 
length of time available.  This site will benefit residents, visitors and travelers in this area.

Affidavit of Engineering Requirement:  AZ3 Silver Creek 
 
The purpose of this report is to explain and demonstrate Verizon Wireless’s significant gap in service and the need for 
the proposed Vertical Bridge site to provide in-building capacity and high-speed data that supports reliable voice and 
data services in the community.   
 
The proposed site, AZ3 Silver Creek, is designed to help provide coverage and additional capacity within the eastern 
area of the White Mountain Lakes community as well as offer some offload to the existing site at Juniper Ridge Resort, 
AZ3 Lynx.  The site will also increase network capacity, which will increase throughput per user. 
 
Without this site, Verizon Wireless will have a significant gap in reliable wireless service in the area of the proposed 
site due to the topography and location of the existing site relative to the needed coverage area.  In fact, the site at the 
Juniper Ridge Resort was designed with the expectation that a future site would be developed on the eastern side of 
White Mountain Lakes.  This two-prong approach was meant to maximize coverage and capacity provided by the sites 
by using two much shorter sites, rather than one large lattice tower.  There is currently a gap in coverage because this 
proposed second site has not yet been built.     
 
The coverage plots in the area with and without the proposed AZ3 Silver Creek site are shown.  Blue areas are areas 
with signal levels higher than -85 dBm which is good enough for in-building coverage.  Green areas are at signal levels 
higher than -95 dBm, which is good enough for in-vehicle coverage.  As you can see from the plots, with this site, the 
areas colored in blue and green are considerably increased.   
 
By adding the solution of AZ3 Silver Creek, Verizon will be completing the next step in the long-term plan to improve 
the coverage in the area.  The Primary benefit will be new and greatly improved coverage on the south and east side of 
White Mountain Lakes and it will also help offload the existing site.  The existing on-air cells’ sizes will reduce which 
results in a smaller number of users per cell, more resources per UE, higher throughput, and better quality of service for 
users in the western and central portions of the community.  
 
From this proposed location, the nearest tower is at the Fire District approximately 1 mile west of the proposed site.  
While this tower does offer excellent height it is directly between the existing site and the proposed location and would 
end up overpowering the existing site while offering inferior system performance in the area around the proposed site.     
 
Verizon’s use of this proposed Vertical Bridge tower will comply with all FAA, FCC, and other applicable regulations.  
 
Attached are the serving cell plots with and without AZ3 Silver Creek, proving cell size reduction.   
 
Thank you,  
 
Darahlee Evans 
RF Engineer

<!-- page 707 -->
Purpose of Notice 
 Vertical Bridge Communications is proposing to place a new 80’ multi-carrier Wireless Facility 
(Monopole) on the Community Center property at 1785 Edmonds Circle.  As part of the Citizen 
Participation process I will be holding a neighborhood meeting July 27th  from 6:00-8:00PM at the 
Community Center. 
 
 You are receiving this notice as you own property within 300’ of the subject parcel at 1785 
Edmonds Circle. 
 
 If you are unable to attend but would like further information, feel free to reach out to me with any 
questions or comments.   
 
Purpose of Application 
 
As part of its ongoing effort to maintain the pre-eminent wireless network in Navajo County, 
Verizon Wireless has engaged Vertical Bridge to develop several sites within the County to improve 
coverage and capacity for Verizon’s network.  This approach is being used to allow for the County to be 
built out faster than if Verizon was developing the sites directly.  Vertical Bridge is one of a few companies 
who have been engaged for different locations throughout the County as part of an overall development 
plan meant to improve rural broadband and overall connectivity.  Vertical Bridge is a large tower 
development and management firm with sites throughout the country and many within Arizona.   
 
This proposal is for a new site in the White Mountain Lake Estates neighborhood.  This site is 
meant to work in conjunction with the existing site to the west at Juniper Ridge.  As I stated when we went 
through the Special Use Permit process for the pole at Juniper Ridge, there would likely need to be a new 
site a few miles east to provide in-building coverage to folks in the eastern part of this development.  That 
is what we are now proposing.   
 
This site is meant to ensure good in-building coverage in this area as well as offer some 
improvement heading north and south along Bourdon Ranch Road.  White Mountain Lakes Estates has 
coverage which drops off quickly on its eastern side as it is currently served by the site at Juniper Ridge.  
Verizon has requested this site to become the primary serving site for the area.  This site will have a 
secondary benefit of offloading capacity at Juniper Ridge which should improve the performance of that 
site for the folks at Juniper Ridge.  It also will integrate with a future site which will be along Bourdon Ranch 
north of the Airport.   
 
While the anchor tenant will be Verizon Wireless, the structure is being developed to handle 
additional carriers if they choose to use it in the future.  Smith Bagley does have a tower a bit over a mile 
west of this location so they would not likely need to collocate but there are two other carriers operating in 
this market. 
 
The primary focus for coverage and capacity was in more densely populated areas and along 
major thoroughfares within the last 5-10 years.  As areas such as this have become more populated and 
technologies have advanced, it is becoming necessary to build additional structures to accommodate 
coverage for residents, visitors and travelers in these areas.  This is a pretty dense area with homes on 
small lots.  Capacity is an issue on the west side of White Mountain Lakes Estates and coverage is an 
issue in the homes on the east side.  This site will help with both of those problems. 
 
 Due to the size and location of the pole at Juniper Ridge it can’t effectively service this area.  The 
existing tower owned by CellOne at the Fire Station is in a spot which makes it a poor option for 
collocation.  It is too close to Juniper Ridge and would overpower that site and is still too far from the east 
side of White Mountain Estates to provide the in-building coverage we need from this site.  As noted 
above, this was actually discussed when Juniper Ridge went through the zoning process.  The plan has 
always been to place multiple sites in this area.

<!-- page 708 -->
Vertical Bridge is requesting a Special Use Permit for a 80’ tall multi-carrier wireless monopole 
within a 50’ x 50’ compound.  There will be ground equipment within the compound.  The height has been 
reduced from the previously proposed 99’ to adhere to the new Wireless Ordinance.       
 
Site Description 
 
The subject parcel is just over 2.5 acres and is surrounded entirely by Edmonds Circle with homes 
on the parcels on the outside of the circle.  This parcel is owned by the Association and used for the 
Community Center/Library as well as the US Post Office.  The Parcel is zoned R1-10 but is one of the few 
non-residential uses in the development.  It is also one of the largest parcels in the development.     
 
The compound will be just east and southeast of the existing building with the community Center 
and the Post office.  This was done to cluster it with the existing buildings yet put it a reasonable distance 
from the surrounding road and homes beyond.  The location allows the pole to be about as far from 
neighboring homes as possible in this community and it is close to the center of the parcel as we could get.    
 
Site History 
 
Verizon Wireless has been working on improving coverage in Navajo County for many years.  That 
often involves a few sites every year.  Now that 5G is being deployed to provide rural broadband coverage 
throughout much of Navajo County, Verizon has a need for several sit es within the next year or two.  
Verizon approached several tower developers about different sites throughout the County.  Vertical Bridge 
is one of the two main tower developers and current ly is loo king at this site.   The east side of this 
community is a targeted location requested by Verizon.   
 
As noted above, Verizon previously developed a site at Juniper Ridge two miles to the west.  It was 
always expected future sites would be needed, especially as technology advanced.  The original proposed 
location for this ring by the carrier was further east , near Bourdon Ranch Road.   Unfortunately , there is 
very little private land in that area, the parcels are very small and there would likely be issues  with the 
airstrip.    When I spoke with the en gineer to determine the desired c overage it became cl ear that this 
location would work to achieve the objectives but we couldn’ t really move any further west as it would 
begin encroaching on and overlapping the site at Juniper Ridge.   
 
I began looking at property records and noticed this parcel was owned by the Association.  It was a 
logical choice as a non- residential use and it also gives you, the neighbors,  an additional opportunity to 
provide feedback on the design.  I devel oped a proposal for the location to keep the pole as far from your  
homes across the circle as reasonably possibl e.  Vertical Bridge entered into a Lease agreement with the 
Association and we are now moving forward with the entitlement process. 
 
Description of Proposal 
 
The proposed site development includes placement of panel antennas on a new 80’ monopole.  
The panel antennas are used for coverage to communicate with phones and other devices.  The 80’ is 
meant to provide a site which meets the needs of Verizon but also leaves space for one to two carriers to 
collocate in the future.  Verizon’s antennas will be at 76’ on the pole to maximize integration with the site at 
Juniper Ridge and the future site north of the Airport.  The pole will be structurally capable of handling 
additional carriers and have usable space available within the compound.   
 
The proposed location is about as close as we could get to the center of the Association’s 2.5 acre 
parcel.  It is more than 1:1 from all property lines and the parcel is surrounded entirely by Edmonds Circle.  
There is currently one home within 200’ of the pole location to the south and a total of 10 homes within 
400’ of the proposed site.  There aren’t other locations within this development which would be able to

<!-- page 709 -->
keep the site further from homes.  The location also is close to commercial power and appears to have 
fiber service available.  Access will come from the Edmonds Circle through the existing parking lot.   
 
The 50’ x 50’ compound is located just ESE of the existing building.  The pole is in the center of the 
compound.  The pole exceeds a 1:1 setback from all property lines. 
   
The Verizon radio equipment will be on a small outdoor platform.  The site will have an emergency 
back-up generator.  The site has commercial power which will come from the existing power pole just SW 
of the main building on the property.   
 
The site will take about 60-90 days to construct, and once complete, will be visited approximately 
once per month for maintenance.  This development is unoccupied and does not involve water or sewer.  
There will not be any changes to existing watercourses or an impact on off-site discharge of rainwater.     
   
 
 
 
Citizen Participation Plan 
 
As previously noted, this site has already been considered and approved by the White Mountain 
Lakes Estates Association.  This was discussed at a Board meeting prior to approval and has been 
discussed further at meetings since the original approval. 
 
This meeting is meant to give you an additional opportunity to provide feedback and be involved in 
the proposed design as a neighborhood stakeholder.  A report of this meeting will be provided to County 
staff.  In addition to this meeting the site will require Public Hearings with Navajo County.  The time(s) and 
date(s) of the County meetings are TBD. 
 
Conclusion 
 
This type of facility requires a Special Use Permit in Navajo County.  This proposal meets the intent 
of the new Wireless Ordinance.  Vertical Bridge will be requesting a Special Use Permit for this proposed 
site for the maximum length of time available.  This site will benefit many of you as well as visitors and 
travelers in this area.

Feedback prior to meeting from Notice:  
I did not receive any direct questions beyond what was raised previously during Community 
Association meetings where this site was discussed several times, including the meeting many 
months ago when they signed the Lease for this site.  I did provide information as to why this site was 
selected, why the existing CellOne Tower wouldn’t work and why we weren’t proposing the site 
outside of this area. 
 
I did join the Community Facebook page in case there was any discussion regarding the site.  There 
were some regular posts about it, primarily they related to health concerns.  There were some people 
in favor of the site on these strings regarding health concerns and a majority opposed to the site 
based on this. 
 
Meeting Notes:  
 
On 7/27 I Arrived at 5:46 and set up.  The meeting room was already open and there were over a 
dozen attendees, even by the time I arrived.  We asked anyone there to sign in and provide written 
comments that I could include in this report. 
 
The Association was kind enough to set this up as a special Board meeting so the Board members 
could be there and they could live-stream the event.  This allowed us to have folks view remotely and 
even ask several questions.   
 
Shortly after 6 we began, and I introduced myself to the attendees.  I gave a short presentation for 
several minutes just providing basic site information regarding the company, the client and how we 
came to this location and proposed design.  At the beginning of the meeting there were about 30 
people in person and a few on the livestream.

<!-- page 716 -->
From my count there were anywhere from 25-30 people in attendance for the majority of the 
time.  There were 27 people on the sign-in sheet.  I did an informal show of hands up front and about 
20 were opposed, 5 were in favor and 4 were undecided.  When I asked later what the reason for 
opposition was and whether it was 5G basically all 20 opposed raised their hands. 
 
 We got through pretty much all of the questions at about 7:50 and ended the meeting promptly 
at 8.  We did have some in-person discussions after the meeting but nothing particularly different than 
what was discussed as a group. 
 
 
 
Questions from the Audience (not necessarily in the order they were asked and each is only listed 
once) 
 
 Will this site have 5G?  This was the main question of the night.  I did make it clear that this 
site would have 4G and 5G when built and tried to explain that 5G is simply a network standard for 
throughput and I also let them know this site would not have MMWave frequency bands. 
 
 Health concerns/Safety:  This was the primary issue and was related to the 5G note above.  
The majority of those opposed to the site did not feel it was safe to have a 5G transmitter in the 
neighborhood.  There did not seem to be concern from most of them regarding older technology 
standards.  The concerns ranged from issues with 5G activating issues with COVID Vaccines to 
cancer to one attendee who recently got a pacemaker but was concerned how it might impact that.  I 
did also mention setbacks regarding pole height and explained that the site is more than its height 
from all property lines, I also mentioned that we will be requesting relief as we are less than 2:1 but 
we are well beyond a full fall zone to stay on property.  I did point out some of the benefits for safety 
and security of having good coverage, being able to call in case of an emergency and even 
mentioned to the person with the pacemaker how my father’s pacemaker uses Bluetooth to 
communicate to his phone and then back to his Doctor to inform the Doctor of any heart issues it is 
sensing regularly. 
 
 How can they ensure the site is operating within its license/they wanted full information on the 
emissions:  I actually suggested that we could have the County require a Pre and Post-EME study on 
the towers.  There are some cities that require these and carriers are able to provide a version which 
can be given to jurisdictions (Scottsdale requires this on sites). 
 
 Why do we need a site if I already have coverage?  I explained that non-Verizon customers 
would not be benefited unless their carrier joined the site in the future.  Most of the attendees were 
either Verizon customers or CellOne customers.  Most of the Cell One customers do have coverage 
and a some of the Verizon customers to the West also have coverage but more than 5 of the folks 
were Verizon customers in support because they don’t have good service near or east of the 
community center. 
 
 Why this location/Why not CellOne tower?  I explained how I came to this spot based on 
direction from the engineering team to locate in this area.  I explained the standard steps of visiting 
the area, looking for any existing verticality, existing site, power poles, large buildings/structures and 
then looking at raw land sites.  I tried to explain why locating on the CellOne tower a mile west would 
not work due its proximity to the existing site and the technological need for several sites.  I spent 
several minutes explaining why the newer technology requires more sites at lower heights, closer to 
users.  There was also concern about whether I approached the association or they approached me.  
I let the attendees know that I simply approached the association because they had the best parcel 
available due to size, setbacks and use.

<!-- page 717 -->
 Will there be more meetings/How can they stay involved?  I let the group know that we’re 
hoping to have the site built by the middle of next year and then Verizon can locate on it but we still 
will be going through the P&Z, BoS and BP processes, and that is assuming the site is not denied.  I 
let them know there would be notices sent and posted as required by the County and the Association 
will also post anything on their FB page.  I mentioned how the attendance at this meeting 
demonstrated that the word was clearly getting out about this site. 
 
 What will the pole look like/Can we do a tree?  This was a question from one of the online 
attendees.  I let them know that we were initially proposing a standard steel monopole but will now be 
proposing a rusticated pole with brown antennas to cut down on the visual impact.  They asked if we 
could do a tree and I explained that a tree, limited to 80’ to the top of branches limits the height quite a 
bit for the first carrier versus a standard 80’ pole and eliminates at least one future collocator. 
 
 What if someone comes to add antennas/change antennas in the future?  I let them know that 
future collocators would need to go through an Administrative Process with the County but changes in 
antennas for existing users would likely not require that process and there is also the possibility that 
additional frequencies could be added without consulting the County.  I did not get into the fact that 
this is handled at the Federal level and the County is limited on its oversite for these types of 
modifications.  They did also separately indicate that they felt the Federal Government was 
overreaching when this should be a local decision.  That came up several times. 
 
 What if this causes more power outages?  I explained that this site uses a similar power set up 
to a standard home.  The fear was that our additional draw would possibly make a fairly unstable 
system even worse. 
 
 Why can’t alternate means be used?  There were two primary suggestions.  The first was 
giving everyone fiber.  I explained that getting fiber connections to every house in a community is 
extremely expensive and, even once it gets there, it typically goes into a router and over the air from 
there.  The second idea I didn’t quite understand as they kept indicating that “Tesla” has developed a 
system to use the ground to transmit signal.  I let them know I was unfamiliar with this and they 
indicated that they felt industry had buried this option. 
 
 Will the tower owner and carrier have “RFM” insurance?  I had not ever heard of this and 
wasn’t sure what it was.  They indicated it was Radio Frequency Measurement insurance.  I was still 
not sure but let them know that the tower owner and all carriers have standard commercial insurance 
policies on these sites. 
 
 Are we aware of the other proposed sites in the area/why don’t we talk to those folks?  I 
actually mentioned that Verizon had tasked another vendor with placing a site about a mile N or this 
location to cover along Bourdon Ranch Road to the north and cover that part of the community and 
that Verizon was using Vertical Bridge to develop a site several miles SE.  They felt I had not been in 
touch with the other vendors.  I let them know I had not spoken to the vendor from Pinnacle proposing 
the site to the North but I did talk to that company (for whom I also do work) after they had their 
neighborhood meeting.  I also mentioned the site VB is doing to the SE several times and am in 
regular communication with Todd Daoust, who is handling that site.  I did explain that we are doing 
these sites at the behest of Verizon and they have close to 20 sites under development in Navajo and 
Apache Counties.  I let them know these developments are done as part of an overall plan and that is 
why these three sites are located where they are. 
 
 How far do these sites cover?  This question flowed from a few others and I let them know that 
a 65’ site in a flat area with the amount of users/density this area has would typically be the primary

<!-- page 718 -->
server for about 1-1.5 miles and the sites would usually be set up to overlap a bit so the network can 
react to spikes in traffic.  This segued into why this site is 2 miles from the current site, why the 
CellOne tower one mile away and between those two sites won’t work and why there is another 
shorter site to the north and a taller site to the SE.  I also mentioned the site we have called Antelope 
which is about 4 miles SSW of this site.  I did have a coverage map showing sites on air and the 
proposed site (it didn’t show the other two proposed sites yet though) 
 
 There was also a question regarding the contract/terms/process for approval:  I let them know 
I wasn’t sure off the top of my head the contract terms and the Board offered to share the info with 
them.  It was also pointed out that the Board approved and signed the agreement about several 
months ago and this site had been discussed prior to signature and a few times at association 
meetings since.

STAFF REPORT  
BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
 
Hearing Date: October 24, 2023 
Case No:  SUP 23-011 
Action:   Special Use Permit 
Applicant/Owner: Destree Development for Vertical Bridge/White Mountain Lake Property 
Owners Assn. 
 
Project Name: US-AZ-5117 Silver Creek Wireless Communication Facility 
 
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 
Recommendation: Staff recommends denial of the Special Use Permit.  If approval is recommended, 
Staff has recommended conditions related to this Special Use Permit. 
 
Location: The property is located in the White Mountain Lakes area on APN # 304-34-328. 
 
Size: 2.50 acres 
 
Supervisor District: III 
 
Zoning: R1-10 (Single-Family Residential Zoning District 10,000 Square Feet Per Dwelling Unit) 
 
Property Owners: White Mountain Lake Property Owners Assn. 
 
Applicant: Destree Development for Vertical Bridge 
 
Representative: Reg Destree 
 
REQUEST DESCRIPTION:  
A request for a Special Use Permit to allow for the construction of a 80’ rusticated monopole wireless 
communication tower and associated facilit ies on a vacant, 2.50-acre parcel, in the White Mountain 
Lakes area. 
 
GENERAL CHARACTER OF NEIGHBORHOOD:  
 
This property is surrounded in all directions by R1 -10, single -family residential zoned properties, 
separated by Edmonds Circle.  There are currently 5 residences that are assessed that sit along Edmonds 
Circle, adjacent to this proposed location.

<!-- page 736 -->
Board of Supervisors              2 | P a g e  
 
 
BACKGROUND/HISTORY: 
 
The subject parcel is lot 328 of the White Mountain Lakes Unit 11 Subdivision, originally designated 
as a community area. 
 
This property currently has a building which is utilized as a community center, library, and U.S. Post 
Office. 
 
At the Thursday, September 21st, 2023 Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission Hearing, the 
Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously recommended denial of this project. 
 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
The proposed project is a n 80’ rusticated monopole wireless communication tower and its associated 
facilities.  The tower, and all associated equipment, will be located in a 50’ x 50’ leased area, surrounded 
by an 8’ chain link fence with a barbed wire topper.  This tower is approximately 113’ from the nearest 
property line, to the south, and approximately 310’ from the furthest property line, to the west. 
 
ZONING DISTRICTS: 
ARTICLE 11 – (R1-10) SINGLE FAMILY RESIDENTIAL ZONING DISTRICT 10,000  
      SQUARE FEET PER DWELLING UNIT 
 
Section 1101 – Purpose.  
 
The principal purpose of this zoning district is to conserve and protect single-family residential 
development where minimum lots of not less than ten-thousand (10,000) square feet in area are 
suitable and appropriate taking into consideration existing conditions, including present use of 
land, present lot sizes, future land use needs, and the availability of public utilities .  Principal 
uses permitted in this zoning district include single-family dwellings, churches, schools, parks, 
playgrounds, and other community facilities. 
 
ZONING ORDINANCE: 
Article 20 – Special Uses and Planned Unit Developments 
 
Section 2001 – Special Uses 
  
The Board of Supervisors may permit as a Special Use the following uses in zoning districts 
from which they are otherwise prohibited by this Ordinance, unless any such use is further 
prohibited by this Article. 
 
34. Television, wireless towe rs, and radio transmitter towers and stations, subject to 
approval by Federal Regulatory Agencies. 
 
Section 2521 – Wireless Communication Facilities

<!-- page 737 -->
Board of Supervisors              3 | P a g e  
 
The purpose of this Section is to establish rules and regulations for the siting of wireless 
communications facilities.  The goals of this Section are to provide for the development of 
wireless communication services County-wide by: 
 
1. Considering the public health, safety, and welfare. 
 
2. Considering impact on adjacent properties. 
 
3. Encouraging configuration which minimizes visual impact through proper siting, design, 
landscape, and camouflage techniques. 
 
COMPREHENSIVE PLAN/AREA PLAN:  
Comprehensive Plan 
 
Land Use Element 
 
Goal 6: Maintain compatible land use patterns while encouraging development. 
 
 Policy 6 -B: Consider, if needed, providing for buffers between different land uses 
 including, but not limited to, setbacks, walls or fences, and landscaping. 
 
▪ The applicant has provid ed plans that indicate they will set back their wireless 
communication facility a minimum of approximately 113’ from all property 
lines.  This does not meet the increased setback requirements of the Navajo 
County Zoning Ordinance for facilities such as thi s one that fall under the 
residential property designation.  
 
 Goal 9: Actively plan to accommodate growth in Navajo County in an appropriate manner. 
 
Policy 9-F: Encourage development/installation of technology improvements including, 
but not limited to, high speed Internet lines and other communications improvements in 
Navajo County. 
 
▪ The applicant is proposing the addition of this wireless communication tower and 
associated facilities in order to provide higher quality wireless service for 
residents, businesses, visitors, and emergency services in this region of Navajo 
County. 
 
Analysis: 
 
This project meets some goals and policies of the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan, but not all.  The 
proposal meets the goal and policy of the Comprehensive Plan related to encouraging communications 
improvements.  However, the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan also encourages buffers that include 
greater setbacks, which are not provided by this project through not following the base requirement for 
residential properties of a two-foot horizontal setback for every one vertical foot of tower height.   
 
Due to not providing the appropriate setback, granting approval of this tower in line with the

<!-- page 738 -->
Board of Supervisors              4 | P a g e  
 
requirements of Section 2521 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance would require a waiver from the 
Navajo County Board of Supervisors for this setback.  For resi dential setback waivers, the Ordinance 
notes: 
 
i. Residential: Towers must be set back 2 feet from any lot line for each 1 foot in height of the 
tower, Including tower and antenna attachments.  
 
1. The 2 foot to 1-foot setback in the residential classification may be reduced on a case-
by-case basis by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors (B.O.S.) if a registered 
engineer can certify that setbacks can be reduced safely. 
 
The proposed tower does meet the maximum height requirement for residentially designated properties, 
which is 80’, which is also the height of the proposed tower. 
 
If a setback waiver is not granted by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, this proposal will not 
meet the requirements of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance. 
 
FINDINGS OF FACT: 
 
1. The item has been properly noticed and posted in compliance with Arizona Revised Statutes 
and Article 29.  
 
This item was posted in the October 4th, 2023 edition of The Holbrook Tribune .  Postcards were 
mailed to neighbors within 300 feet of the property and the subject property was posted with public 
hearing notices. 
 
2. The proposal is in compliance with the Comprehensive Plan. 
 
The proposed project does not meet all goals of the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan, as outlined 
in this report. 
 
3. The proposed use is compatible with the permissible uses in the zoning district in which the 
property is located. 
 
The proposed use is compatible with permissible uses within the R1-10 zoning district. 
 
4. The proposed use is  compatible with the current and likely future uses of properties in the 
vicinity of the proposed use.  
 
The proposed use is compatible with nearby uses, of which the majority are vacant, single-family 
residential zoned properties. 
 
5. The proposed use will have minimal adverse effects on the public health, safety, and general 
welfare of properties in the vicinity of the proposed use. 
 
There should  be minimal adverse effects on the public health, safety, and general welfare of 
properties in the vicinity of the proposed use.

PLANNING AND ZONING COMMISSION/STAFF RECOMMENDATION:  
 
The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously recommended denial of this Special Use 
Permit 
 
Based upon the fact that this proposal does not meet all relevant goals of the Navajo County Comprehensive 
Plan and requires a waiver to setback standards which can only be granted by the Navajo Co unty Board of 
Supervisors, Planning and Development Services Staff recommends denial of this Special Use Permit. 
 
If the Navajo County Board of Supervisors approves this Special Use Permit, Navajo County Planning and 
Development Services Staff would recommend the following conditions:  
 
1. This Special Use Permit shall permit 1 (one) monopole wireless communication tower, not to 
exceed 80 feet in height, and accessory structures necessary for the operation of the tower on 
the subject property. 
 
2. The applicant shall obtain a Building Permit from Navajo County for such tower and facilities 
prior to commencing construction. 
 
3. The applicant shall meet all State and Federal requirements concerning communication towers 
prior to any building permits being issued. 
 
4. The tower shall be constructed as a monopole, as indicated in the supplied plans.  The owner of 
the tower shall maintain the tower, antennae as necessary. 
 
5. A fence of material acceptable to the Planning and Development Services Director shall be constructed 
to enclose the base of the tower and necessary accessory structures.  
 
6. A Geotechnical Report for the Access Easement shall be submitted and approved.

<!-- page 740 -->
Board of Supervisors              6 | P a g e  
 
7. The permitted Special Use shall be allowed to occur per the attached/approved site plan.  Any 
expansion or change of the Special Use shall require an amendment to this permit. 
 
8. If the permitted Special Use is not utilized within a twelve (12) month period, from the date of 
Board approval, this permit shall become null and void. 
 
9. Should the operator decide to abandon the use of the tower, they shall notify Navajo County 
Planning and Development Services that the tower is no longer being utilized. 
 
10. If the tower is no longer being utilized, the property owner and/or applicant shall cause, at their 
expense, the removal of all components of this tower within a 90-day period. 
 
11. The owner shall provide reasonable cooperation to other public and private users who may be 
interested in collocation on this tower and shall consider such colloca tion upon commercially 
reasonable terms, unless such collocation is not technically feasible. 
 
12. This Special Use Permit shall be personal to the permittee and applicable only to the specific use and 
to the specific property for which it is issued. Upon comp letion and final inspection by the Planning 
and Development Services Director (or designee) of any authorized structures, signifying that all 
zoning and site development requirements imposed in connection with the permit have been satisfied, 
the Special Us e Permit shall thereafter be transferable and shall run with the land, whereupon the 
maintenance of special conditions imposed by the permit, as well as the compliance with other 
provisions of this title, shall be the responsibility of the property owner. 
 
13. This Special Use Permit and the subject site shall be reviewed and inspected by Planning and 
Development Staff on the fifth (5 th) anniversary of Board of Supervisors approval and every five (5) 
years thereafter to ensure the site is being utilized as approved and is in compliance with all conditions 
contained herein.  If the subject site is found to be out of compliance with these conditions, this Special 
Use Permit and its privileges may be revoked.

Zoning Commission, where the item was recommended for approval to the Navajo County
Board of Supervisors by a vote of 5-0, subject to conditions.

Navajo County Board of Supervisors, where it was approved by a vote of 4-0, subject to the
conditions of Resolution # 32-22.

Permit Amendment, subject to the conditions contained within the Staff Report.
